text: Who is known as the 'Brains of the Katipunan'?
explanation: Emilio Jacinto served as the chief adviser and writer for the Katipunan.

text: Who was the leader of the longest revolt in Philippine history against Spanish rule, lasting for 85 years?
explanation: Francisco Dagohoy led the longest revolt in Bohol (1744–1829) after a priest refused to give his brother a Christian burial.

text: What was the name of the secret society founded by Andres Bonifacio in 1892 that sought independence from Spain?
explanation: The Kataastaasan, Kagalanggalangang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan (KKK) was founded in Tondo, Manila.

text: Who is known as the 'Sublime Paralytic' and the 'Brains of the Revolution'?
explanation: Apolinario Mabini served as the chief adviser to Emilio Aguinaldo despite being paralyzed by polio.

text: The execution of which three Filipino priests in 1872 ignited the flames of Philippine nationalism?
explanation: The martyrdom of Gomez, Burgos, and Zamora (Gomburza) inspired Jose Rizal and the Propaganda Movement.

text: What was the title of Jose Rizal's first novel, published in 1887, which exposed the social cancer of Spanish rule?
explanation: Noli Me Tangere (Touch Me Not) was published in Berlin and shifted the focus toward Philippine reforms.

text: On what date was Philippine independence from Spain proclaimed in Kawit, Cavite?
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed independence on June 12, 1898, from the window of his mansion.

text: Who was the youngest General of the Philippine Revolutionary Army, known as the 'Boy General'?
explanation: Gregorio del Pilar died defending Tirad Pass to allow Aguinaldo to escape from American forces.

text: What treaty was signed in 1898 where Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States for $20 million?
explanation: The Treaty of Paris ended the Spanish-American War and transferred Philippine sovereignty to the USA.

text: Who was the first President of the Commonwealth of the Philippines?
explanation: Manuel L. Quezon served as the first president of the Commonwealth from 1935 until his death in 1944.

text: What event on April 9, 1942, involved the forced march of Filipino and American POWs under the Japanese?
explanation: The Bataan Death March began in Mariveles, Bataan, and ended at Camp O'Donnell in Tarlac.

text: Who was the first female President of the Philippines?
explanation: Corazon Aquino took office after the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution ousted Ferdinand Marcos.

text: Which President moved the Independence Day celebration from July 4 to June 12?
explanation: Diosdado Macapagal signed the proclamation in 1962 to honor the actual 1898 declaration.

text: Who was the 'Brains of the Katipunan' and author of the Kartilya ng Katipunan?
explanation: Emilio Jacinto was a law student who became the primary advisor and writer for Bonifacio's KKK.

text: Which explorer gave the name 'Las Islas Filipinas' to the archipelago in honor of Prince Philip II of Spain?
explanation: Ruy Lopez de Villalobos gave the name specifically to Leyte and Samar during his 1543 expedition.

text: What was the name of the first Spanish settlement established by Legazpi in 1565?
explanation: Cebu was the first permanent Spanish settlement, initially named Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus.

text: Who was the great orator of the Propaganda Movement and the first editor of 'La Solidaridad'?
explanation: Graciano Lopez Jaena founded the paper in Barcelona in 1889 to advocate for Philippine reforms.

text: During which battle in 1521 was Ferdinand Magellan killed by the forces of Lapu-Lapu?
explanation: The Battle of Mactan took place on April 27, 1521, where Lapu-Lapu resisted Spanish intrusion.

text: What was the Japanese-sponsored government (1943–1945) also known as?
explanation: It is referred to as the Second Republic, headed by Jose P. Laurel during the occupation.

text: Who was the 'Great Plebeian' who founded the Katipunan?
explanation: Andres Bonifacio is called the Great Plebeian because he came from a humble background.

text: The 'Cry of Pugad Lawin' involved what symbolic act by the Katipuneros?
explanation: The tearing of the 'cedula' (tax certificate) symbolized their refusal to obey Spanish authority.

text: Who was the Filipino general known as the 'Hero of Tirad Pass'?
explanation: Gregorio del Pilar died at the age of 24 while defending the pass against American troops.

text: Which President is known for the 'Filipino First Policy'?
explanation: Carlos P. Garcia implemented this policy to give local businessmen priority over foreign investors.

text: Who was the last President of the Commonwealth and the first President of the Third Republic?
explanation: Manuel Roxas was inaugurated on July 4, 1946, when the US granted full independence.

text: What was the name of the newspaper used by the Propagandists to air their grievances in Spain?
explanation: La Solidaridad was the mouthpiece of Filipino reformers in Europe.

text: Who was the 'Champion of the Masses' whose presidency ended in a tragic plane crash?
explanation: Ramon Magsaysay died in 1957 when the presidential plane 'Mt. Pinatubo' crashed in Cebu.

text: In what year did President Ferdinand Marcos declare Martial Law through Proclamation No. 1081?
explanation: Martial Law was officially signed on September 21, 1972, though announced to the public later.

text: Who was the founder of the Aglipayan Church (Philippine Independent Church)?
explanation: Gregorio Aglipay, a former Catholic priest, co-founded the church in 1902 during the revolution.

text: What was the name of the movement that fought against the Japanese in Central Luzon during WWII?
explanation: The Hukbalahap (Hukbo ng Bayan Laban sa Hapon) was a peasant-based guerrilla army.

text: Which Spanish Governor-General was responsible for the execution of Jose Rizal?
explanation: Camilo de Polavieja signed the death warrant for Rizal, leading to his execution in 1896.

text: Where was Jose Rizal exiled for four years before his execution?
explanation: Rizal lived in Dapitan from 1892 to 1896, where he practiced medicine and built a school.

text: In what year was the Philippine Declaration of Independence proclaimed?
explanation: Independence from Spain was declared on June 12, 1898.

text: Who authored the novel 'Noli Me Tangere'?
explanation: Jose Rizal wrote 'Noli Me Tangere' as a critique of Spanish colonial rule.

text: Which event marked the start of the Philippine Revolution against Spain?
explanation: The Cry of Pugad Lawin is traditionally regarded as the symbolic start of the revolution.

text: Who became the first President of the Commonwealth of the Philippines?
explanation: Manuel L. Quezon served as the first Commonwealth President in 1935.

text: Which event is generally considered the beginning of Spanish colonization in the Philippines?
explanation: The arrival of Ferdinand Magellan in 1521 marked the first contact with Spain and the beginning of Spanish involvement in the Philippines.

choices.text: The opening of the Suez Canal

text: Who ordered the execution of Gomburza in 1872?
explanation: Governor-General Rafael Izquierdo ordered the execution of Gomburza following the Cavite Mutiny.

text: Which movement sought reforms from Spain through peaceful means?
explanation: The Propaganda Movement aimed to secure reforms for Filipinos through peaceful advocacy and writings.

text: What was the primary objective of the Katipunan?
explanation: The Katipunan aimed to gain independence from Spain through armed revolution.

choices.text: To request representation in the Spanish Cortes
To establish trade relations with Spain

text: Where was the Philippine Declaration of Independence proclaimed on June 12, 1898?
explanation: The Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in Kawit, Cavite.

text: Which treaty formally ended the Spanish-American War?
explanation: The Treaty of Paris of 1898 ended the Spanish-American War and transferred the Philippines to the United States.

text: Who was the first President of the First Philippine Republic?
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo served as the first President of the First Philippine Republic.

text: Which law provided for the gradual granting of independence to the Philippines by the United States?
explanation: The Tydings–McDuffie Act established the Commonwealth of the Philippines and set a timetable for independence.

text: Who was the President of the Commonwealth of the Philippines?
explanation: Manuel L. Quezon served as President of the Commonwealth government.

text: Which event marked the start of Japanese occupation in the Philippines during World War II?
explanation: Japanese forces invaded the Philippines shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941.

choices.text: Declaration of Manila as an open city

text: Who served as President of the Philippines during the Japanese occupation?
explanation: Jose P. Laurel served as President of the Second Philippine Republic under Japanese occupation.

text: What was the significance of the Battle of Leyte Gulf?
explanation: The Battle of Leyte Gulf was the largest naval battle of World War II and led to the liberation of the Philippines.

choices.text: It marked the start of Japanese occupation
It led to the return of General MacArthur

text: When did the Philippines gain full independence from the United States?
explanation: The Philippines gained full independence on July 4, 1946.

text: Who was the first President of the Third Philippine Republic?
explanation: Manuel Roxas became the first President of the independent Republic of the Philippines in 1946.

text: Which Philippine president was known for his strong anti-corruption campaign and populist leadership?
explanation: Ramon Magsaysay was known for his integrity, accessibility, and anti-corruption stance.

text: Which event marked the declaration of Martial Law in the Philippines?
explanation: President Ferdinand Marcos declared Martial Law in 1972 through Proclamation No. 1081.

text: Which event led to the end of the Marcos regime in 1986?
explanation: The EDSA People Power Revolution peacefully ended the Marcos dictatorship.

text: Who became President after the 1986 People Power Revolution?
explanation: Corazon C. Aquino became President following the EDSA Revolution.

text: Which constitution is currently in effect in the Philippines?
explanation: The 1987 Constitution was ratified after the EDSA Revolution and remains in effect today.

text: Who is recognized as the national hero of the Philippines?
explanation: Jose Rizal is recognized as the national hero due to his writings and influence on Philippine nationalism.

text: What was the primary purpose of the Malolos Congress of 1898?
explanation: The Malolos Congress was convened to draft the first Philippine Constitution and establish a republican government.

text: Which Philippine president implemented the New Society (Bagong Lipunan) program?
explanation: President Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr. introduced the New Society as part of his governance during Martial Law.

text: Which event is considered the first armed conflict between Filipino revolutionaries and American forces?
explanation: The Battle of San Juan Bridge in 1899 marked the beginning of the Philippine-American War.

text: What was the significance of the Jones Law of 1916?
explanation: The Jones Law promised eventual independence to the Philippines and reorganized its legislature.

text: Which Filipino hero was executed at Bagumbayan (Luneta) on December 30, 1896?
explanation: Dr. José Rizal was executed by Spanish authorities, an event that intensified the Philippine Revolution.
